column1: # Shared fork-layer rename table: NeoForge 21.11 -> 26.1.2 (Minecraft 26.1.2; NeoForge 26.1.2). Applied FIRST (nearest) on the
# 1.21.1 text, then the 1.21.11/1.21.10/... tables on whatever it left -- so a row here is written against the ORIGINAL
# 1.21.1 spelling. A rename row reaches the AUTHORS' files only: never an overlay (CATALOG §W8) nor a shared helper, so an
# overlay inherited from a parent target that still has the 1.21.x shape is fixed by hand in targets/26.1.2/java.
#!exhaustive  # shared library: most forks use only some of these rows
# ---- Block light (CATALOG M64): 1.21.2 dropped getLightBlock's BlockGetter/BlockPos and 26.1 renamed it getLightDampening
# (BlockBehaviour and BlockStateBase alike; unchanged through 26.3). An override left as getLightBlock overrides nothing
# and vanilla's default runs (15 for a solid render, else 0 if it propagates skylight, else 1). A body that read the
# dropped level/pos fails to compile, loudly, rather than being guessed at.
# ---- Properties.hasPostProcess(StatePredicate) is postProcess(PostProcess) in 26.1: the hook returns the position to
# post-process after world generation (vanilla's Blocks.postProcessSelf returns pos) or null for none. Only the
# always-true predicate is rewritten; any other predicate is left for the compiler to name.
